newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania police disperse anti-government protest.
newsitem.headline: Albania police disperse anti-government protest.

text.p: About 3,000 Albanians pushed past police to demonstrate in Tirana's main square on Sunday, but truncheon-wielding officers broke up an attempt to march down a central boulevard, witnesses said.

A crowd led by opposition party leaders pierced police lines to reach Skanderbeg square, scene of a 1990 uprising that toppled the communist regime, shouting: "The police are with us, the government is a thief".
Hundreds more joined the crowd to try to move down the Martyrs of the Nation boulevard but were halted by police grouped behind the equestrian statue of Albania's mediaeval hero, Skanderbeg.
"The police mainly just used their bodies to push people away but there were a few incidents of batons being used," one witness said.

Albanian President Sali Berisha and his conservative Democratic Party government were severely criticised by foreign governments last May when police beat up opposition leaders and protesters around Skanderbeg Square in a demonstration against alleged election rigging by the Democrats.

Less than half an hour after Sunday's protest began, plainclothes police intervened as opposition leaders tried to address the throng, smashing their megaphones and holding them back from a platform in the centre of the square.
Foreign diplomats watched the scene from the balcony of the Hotel Tirana International which overlooks the square.
Police beat shields with their batons to try to scare demonstrators away from the main avenue but some struck out at protesters, witnesses said. Some were seen with bloodied faces.
Water cannon were on standby but were not used.
While police tactics were more restrained than during last year's anti-government protest, their strategy of keeping groups from assembling in Skanderbeg Square appeared to be working.
Within an hour the main crowd had dispersed but hundreds continued to mill around streets fanning out from the square.

The protest was called by three opposition parties -- the Socialists, centre-right Democratic Alliance and centre-left Social Democrats -- following a week of minor demonstrations against collapsing pyramid investment schemes in which hundreds of people have lost their life savings.

"We don't need the parties, we need our money back," one protester shouted after being called on to follow opposition leaders. "Berisha where is our money? Down with the dictatorship," shouted others.
Pyramid schemes boomed in the Balkan nation after the fall of communism in 1990, luring thousands of Albanians into selling homes, land and livestock with promises of big returns.

Three investment groups have collapsed in the past few weeks in Albania, Europe's poorest country. Infuriated investors clashed with police on Wednesday in a demonstration over the investment projects.
Berisha vowed on Saturday to crack down on pyramid investment schemes but warned the opposition against exploiting anger to try to destabilise the ex-communist state.
